narrative.overview: A Git history viewer that behaves like glass instruments over a lit-white glow field: the data sits on translucent smoked panes, and the colour behind them is what makes each pane visible. Depth comes from the background and glass tinting, almost never from drop shadows. Calm and precise — hierarchy is drawn through a bouncy type ladder (16px titles, 14px body, 10.5px data labels) rather than decoration, and every metric object speaks in a JetBrains Mono micro-voice. One muted violet accent (Dusty Iris, slightly greyed, never neon) carries meaning, and a fixed family of eight muted lane hues owns the commit graph, where colour is topology, not decoration. The original saturated aurora canvas was replaced by a white canvas with soft glowing corners (dark theme: white halos on the deep canvas); glass-over-a-glow-field carries, the sunset saturation does not.
keyCharacteristics: Glass layers everywhere (hairline border + glass fill + backdrop blur + ambient shadow), always legible edges
Tokens-only theming: components reference --color-* variables; .dark re-points them
Lane-chromatic graph: a node, its segments and its ref pills always share laneColor(k)
Micro-mono for data; bold titles carry the hierarchy
Desktop-only: responsive means user-resizable panes, not breakpoints

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Components never hardcode hex; they reference --color-* tokens, and .dark does the theming. Sanctioned exceptions are the mock-palette syntax schemes and settings theme previews.

rules.name: Dark-Chromatic Rule
rules.body: Colour belongs to the lane: a node, its line segments and ref pills all wear laneColor(k); a shifting line takes the new lane's hue at the bend.

rules.name: The Ink-Pair Rule
rules.body: Every loud colour carries a *-ink companion for readable small text; white-on-violet and ink-pair-on-tint are the only pairings.

rules.name: The Visible Ladder Rule
rules.body: The jump between type ranks must be felt: 16 > 14 > 12.5 > 10.5px with weight doing the separating; merge ranks that render the same size.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Anything git produced numerically or as a hash is JetBrains Mono; prose never is.

rules.name: The Depth-From-Field Rule
rules.body: A new surface gets glass + the aurora field, never a heavier shadow; add a different glass layer, not a bigger shadow.

rules.name: The Var-Route Rule
rules.body: Shadows ship only through the panel-shadow / soft-shadow custom utilities — Tailwind v4 inlines @theme literals, so its shadow-panel/shadow-soft would silently never theme in .dark.

dos: Do reference --color-* tokens from components only, and re-point them under .dark
Do ship shadows exclusively through the panel-shadow / soft-shadow custom utilities
Do tint any interactive element floating on the aurora with bg-glass-soft + backdrop-blur-md
Do pair a loud colour with its *-ink variant for small text
Do keep binary components round (pill/toggle) and chrome square-ish (8-16px)
Do build data rows as fixed grids out of tableLayout.ts constants; 32px per row, 16px per lane
donts: Don't reintroduce the saturated aurora canvas — it was replaced by white canvas + corner glows (light) / white halos on deep canvas (dark)
Don't use Tailwind's shadow-panel / shadow-soft or type border-1.5 — use panel-shadow / soft-shadow and border-[1.5px]
Don't invent a second accent family or a saturated mock-palette colour outside the sanctioned theme-preview syntax scopes
Don't hide an affordance behind hover only — visible at rest, strengthened on hover, never hover-only discovery
Don't put a dark: variant in a component span; add a token instead
Don't colour a component with a hue the lane didn't earn; graph colour is lane-owned via laneColor(k)
Don't let a pill or line carry its previous lane's colour after a bend
